Bitcoin's recent performance suggests a trend moving away from the $200,000 target. The cryptocurrency has fallen about 27% over the past year and is down 5.3% so far in 2026, meaning buyers are currently at a loss in both time frames. On a brighter note, Bitcoin has risen 29% over the last 90 days, indicating a solid short-term rebound, but it's still down for the year overall. Over the past five years, Bitcoin has gained approximately 44%. While this is a healthy long-term increase, it's still less than one-third of the 141% needed to reach the target in the next 18 months. To reach the $200,000 target, Bitcoin must first recover and exceed its previous all-time high of $126,080. Currently, Bitcoin is trading 34.2% below that peak and needs to rise 52% just to get back there. Once it hits that milestone, Bitcoin will need to climb another 59% to reach $200,000, well beyond its prior high. For Bitcoin to realistically aim for $200,000, three key steps must occur in order: One-Year Recovery: The 90-day rebound must become a full-year recovery to erase the current 27% decline over the past year. If Bitcoin remains down over this longer timeframe, sellers will dominate the market. Breaking the Previous High: Bitcoin must clear the 52% barrier to reclaim its all-time high of $126,080 and stay above it. Historically, old highs can act as resistance points, where sellers previously overwhelmed buyers. Any price spike that fails to hold above this mark would not count. Increasing Demand: Demand for Bitcoin must grow faster than the halving alone. Since many investors already know about the supply cut, any additional momentum must come from new investment, including a return of demand for Bitcoin ETFs, which saw $731 million in outflows in early October. Given the current landscape, Bitcoin hitting $200,000 by the halving in April 2028 seems unlikely. Hitting this target requires a 141% increase from around $83,000 in just 18 months, even as Bitcoin is down 27% over the past year. If the first two steps don't materialize, Bitcoin may still struggle to break back above its prior high by the time the halving arrives, putting the $200,000 goal out of reach. For Bitcoin holders, the $126,080 record is the key level to watch. If Bitcoin breaks through this level and stays above it well before reaching block 1,050,000, the prospect of hitting $200,000 becomes more realistic, despite the need for an additional 59% rise. Until then, investors may want to treat the $200,000 target as a long-term goal rather than an imminent one. extraction.body: The following is the transcript of the interview with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin that aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Oct. 11, 2026.MARGARET BRENNAN: Good morning, and welcome to Face the Nation. We've got a lot of politics ahead, but we want to start with a quick update on the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall Friday night and resulted in the deaths of four people. For that update, we turn to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. What is needed?SECRETARY OF HOMELAND SECURITY MARKWAYNE MULLIN: Well, we were in touch with the- with all the governors that are affected and might be affected by the continuing storm moving across the nation. Cam Hamilton, who is our director of FEMA, we started pre-positioning assets into every state and working closely with their emergency responders. Right now, from the conversation I've had with each governor, they're in good shape. What's interesting about this area is they're- while they may not have been hit with storms real bad the last two years, they work really, really good together. When I was talking to Governor Kemp from, you know, from Georgia, he was talking about his relationship with Ron DeSantis. When we're dealing with the other governors, they were talking about how they're cooperating with sending assets to the areas that are affected without power to get the- the power restored. FEMA is standing by responding with- with life-saving responses. We were, you know, you never can be fully prepared for- for a storm like this, but I can tell you that the coordination from- from the Oval Office with President Trump's leadership to the- to the governors to the county first responders, we're all working very closely together.MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, we hope everyone in that pathway is safe. There have been at least 30 DHS officer-involved shootings under the Trump administration, according to CBS's tally of events here. There was this incident last week in New York City, and the NYPD did release security video that shows a man dressed as a civilian with a gun drawn approaching a car and then punching in the window. I know you have said there were other DHS ICE officers in the area who were put at risk by the driver, but just to clarify events, when are you going to release the body cameras worn by those officers?SEC. MULLIN: Well, Margaret, what you're seeing is a pole cam. What you're not seeing is actual- the audio footage or a different angle where you have multiple officers that are actually approaching this- this individual named Oscar with a long, very long, extensive rap sheet. He's only been in the country for- for three years, and he has a rap sheet of four charges of felony robbery, two charges of felony assault, felony larceny, misdemeanor assault, possession of- of weapons, possession of stolen property, two felony charges of drugless- of dangerous drugs, and strong gang affiliation that- that has direct or indirect knowledge of- of a CBP officer that was shot last year. We had approached him just like any other undercover agency that's out there, from local, state, federal, or- or county that has undercover officers. He decided that he was going to accelerate and try to evade again. We had taken every precaution to try to keep that from happening, and- and unfortunately, this took place. But as far as--(CROSSTALK)MARGARET BRENNAN: You said they were wearing body cameras. MULLIN:--the information being released--MARGARET BRENNAN: When will you release that footage?(END CROSSTALK)SEC. MULLIN: As far- Margaret, as far as the information being released, FBI and HSI is going to do the investigation. When it's completed, we'll release all the information.MARGARET BRENNAN: Okay. There was that five-year-old you just mentioned. Given that rap sheet and how long you'd been monitoring, how come those officers didn't notice that a child was put in that car?SEC. MULLIN: Well, what- our understanding is- is he drove into the neighborhood. He knew the police was looking for him because, like I said, he just evaded a month ago. He's the one that decided to accelerate and- and ram into another vehicle with his five-year-old in the vehicle, and then tried to accelerate towards other police officers. That's- that is that tells you the type of character that Oscar is, and yet somehow the mayor is out there protesting about this, but yet seven days ago, when NYPD officer got stabbed in the same neighborhood by- by criminals that they released, by the way, Oscar had been released multiple times back onto the streets. Not one time did the governor, not one time did the mayor have a press conference or talk about--(CROSSTALK)MARGARET BRENNAN: They did release a statement and visit the officer in the hospital. MULLIN: --how awful it was that these criminals are stabbing NYPD officers. (END CROSSTALK)SEC. MULLIN: That's right.MARGARET BRENNAN: But I think we're all thankful, as I'm sure you are, that that five-year-old was not harmed. MULLIN: -- Absolutely-- MARGARET BRENNAN: -- about this, though. MULLIN: -- It's frustrating, though, Margaret, because this guy should have never been on the streets because we had asked- we had had a detainer on him and asked the New York City to hand him over to us when they had him on in- in their possession, he was on probation.

extraction.body: Heading into the final quarter of 2026, crypto investors have some tough choices to make as they diversify their portfolios. Should they double down on Hyperliquid ( HYPE +0.84% ) , which is up a stunning 236% this year and now has the support of the Trump administration ? Or should they look for another high-flying altcoin that might benefit from the passage of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act? Or there's a third option: They could go with a proven winner that's having a bit of an off-year in 2026, down 9%. I'm talking, of course, about Bitcoin ( BTC +0.68% ) , which is now coming off one of its best Augusts ever and could be primed for a final year-end rally. What makes Bitcoin stand out from every other cryptocurrency is its unique mix of upside potential and downside protection. As BlackRock recently noted, Bitcoin has a unique duality: It is both a "risk-on" and a "risk-off" asset. In terms of upside potential, all you have to do is look at the numbers over the past decade. Bitcoin has delivered truly exponential gains over that time period. On Sept. 1, 2016, Bitcoin was trading at just $572. Today, it trades at just under $80,000. Bitcoin has consistently delivered triple-digit returns over a sustained period. In fact, the outlier years are the ones when Bitcoin does not double in value. Case in point: In six of the past 10 years, Bitcoin has delivered returns of 92% or higher. No wonder Bitcoin's price growth has been off the charts. In terms of downside protection, Bitcoin can serve as a unique portfolio diversifier . As BlackRock points out, Bitcoin has historically been uncorrelated with major asset classes. That has made it a phenomenal hedge, because Bitcoin can zig when other assets zag. In addition, Bitcoin has proven its worth as a safe-haven asset during periods of extreme geopolitical and macroeconomic instability. For good reason, many investors think about Bitcoin as "digital gold." As former Fed Chair Jerome Powell has noted, Bitcoin could be a modern form of gold that can (theoretically) preserve its value over time. Right now, Bitcoin is trading at just under $80,000. But plenty of investors think it could reach $100,000 this year. And, from there, the sky is the limit. Investment firm Bernstein , for example, thinks Bitcoin will hit $150,000 by mid-2027 and $300,000 by 2029. Others have far loftier targets. For example, Cathie Wood of Ark Invest is convinced that Bitcoin could be trading above $1 million by the end of 2030. With that in mind, Bitcoin is the one cryptocurrency that's at the top of my investment shopping list right now. It has a unique mix of upside potential and downside protection that can help it outperform in nearly any type of market environment. Dominic Basulto has positions in Bitcoin. extraction.body: Heading into the final quarter of 2026, crypto investors have some tough choices to make as they diversify their portfolios. Should they double down on Hyperliquid ( HYPE +0.84% ) , which is up a stunning 236% this year and now has the support of the Trump administration ? Or should they look for another high-flying altcoin that might benefit from the passage of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act? Or there's a third option: They could go with a proven winner that's having a bit of an off-year in 2026, down 9%. I'm talking, of course, about Bitcoin ( BTC +0.68% ) , which is now coming off one of its best Augusts ever and could be primed for a final year-end rally. What makes Bitcoin stand out from every other cryptocurrency is its unique mix of upside potential and downside protection. As BlackRock recently noted, Bitcoin has a unique duality: It is both a "risk-on" and a "risk-off" asset. In terms of upside potential, all you have to do is look at the numbers over the past decade. Bitcoin has delivered truly exponential gains over that time period. On Sept. 1, 2016, Bitcoin was trading at just $572. Today, it trades at just under $80,000. Bitcoin has consistently delivered triple-digit returns over a sustained period. In fact, the outlier years are the ones when Bitcoin does not double in value. Case in point: In six of the past 10 years, Bitcoin has delivered returns of 92% or higher. No wonder Bitcoin's price growth has been off the charts. In terms of downside protection, Bitcoin can serve as a unique portfolio diversifier . As BlackRock points out, Bitcoin has historically been uncorrelated with major asset classes. That has made it a phenomenal hedge, because Bitcoin can zig when other assets zag. In addition, Bitcoin has proven its worth as a safe-haven asset during periods of extreme geopolitical and macroeconomic instability. For good reason, many investors think about Bitcoin as "digital gold." As former Fed Chair Jerome Powell has noted, Bitcoin could be a modern form of gold that can (theoretically) preserve its value over time. Right now, Bitcoin is trading at just under $80,000. But plenty of investors think it could reach $100,000 this year. And, from there, the sky is the limit. Investment firm Bernstein , for example, thinks Bitcoin will hit $150,000 by mid-2027 and $300,000 by 2029. Others have far loftier targets. For example, Cathie Wood of Ark Invest is convinced that Bitcoin could be trading above $1 million by the end of 2030. With that in mind, Bitcoin is the one cryptocurrency that's at the top of my investment shopping list right now. It has a unique mix of upside potential and downside protection that can help it outperform in nearly any type of market environment. Dominic Basulto has positions in Bitcoin. Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) reaching $1 million and XRP (CRYPTO:XRP) hitting $10 are two major price points that many holders frequently discuss when looking ahead to the next cycle for both cryptocurrencies. While $1 million for Bitcoin may sound astronomical and $10 for XRP seems more achievable, the gap between these two targets may not be as wide as it appears.

For perspective, Bitcoin needs to grow 12.1 times from its current price of $82,965 as of October 11, 2026. In contrast, XRP needs to grow only 7.2 times from its current price of $1.39. This means XRP has a shorter distance to climb.

When comparing price targets, it's essential to understand how far each cryptocurrency must rise to meet those goals. Each target is roughly comparable to past price surges of each coin, which lends credibility to the potential for achieving these numbers. However, it's important not to overlook the overall market dynamics required for both cryptocurrencies to reach their targets.

Market capitalization—calculated by multiplying the cryptocurrency's price by the number of coins in circulation—gives a clearer picture of the asset's worth and what it takes to reach a specific price target.

As of now, Bitcoin's market value is around $1.67 trillion with roughly 20.1 million coins in circulation. For Bitcoin to reach $1 million per coin, its total market value would skyrocket to about $20.1 trillion. This figure represents an unprecedented demand for funds in the cryptocurrency market.

On the other hand, XRP has about 63.1 billion coins available. For XRP to reach $10, its market value would be only about $631 billion. Even at that price, XRP would be only about 38% of Bitcoin's current market value, meaning that XRP at $10 would still be smaller than Bitcoin is now.

When considering both the required multiple and market demand, XRP clearly comes out ahead. It requires a smaller growth multiple and substantially less new investment than Bitcoin, which needs a much larger market influx.

Both coins have to overcome several price levels before reaching their targets. XRP has dropped 41.3% over the past year and must first reclaim the $1.84 mark, where it started 2026. This represents a 32.4% increase from its current price. The next level to beat is $2.38, 71.2% above its current price. Only then would $10 be a serious possibility.

Similarly, Bitcoin must move past certain price thresholds. It started 2026 at $87,498, 5.5% above its current trading price, and was $110,769 a year earlier, 33.5% higher than where it trades now. Both critical price points are still well above Bitcoin's current price.

Based on the analysis, XRP hitting $10 appears to be the more achievable target of the two. XRP's required 7.2-fold increase is far less daunting than Bitcoin's 12.1-fold rise. Additionally, XRP's market value would only need to reach around $631 billion, compared to the staggering $20.1 trillion needed for Bitcoin.

Investors can watch key price levels to gauge potential moves toward these targets. If XRP fails to climb back above $1.84, a move to $10 becomes less likely. A close above $2.38 would signal that buyers are responding to the potential of reaching higher targets. In contrast, if Bitcoin surpasses $110,769 while XRP struggles, discussions about Bitcoin reaching $1 million could gain traction.

extraction.body: Get ready to pay for more expensive iCloud+ plans. With the release of iOS 27, Apple is deploying its much-anticipated Siri AI suite of features across its software ecosystem. One noteworthy change is coming to Apple HomeKit, as the Cupertino company injects Apple Intelligence into its home security camera system. The upgrade launches Apple's video summary feature, where you can generate descriptions of videos caught on your home security system. The feature groups together related clips across multiple cameras for a comprehensive picture of a specific event, allowing you to easily review events that occur at your home. For instance, Apple's press release announcing the feature shows a man identified as Robert arriving at a home with a fruit bowl of fruit, an example showcasing how HomeKit's Apple Intelligence and Face Recognition software work together to generate these summaries. You can also search these recordings using natural language queries, as well as group similar videos together to reduce notifications. And while your willingness to invite yet another AI algorithm into your life may vary, it's no doubt that the new feature is another sign of AI's continued push into modern smart homes . Notably, the feature won't be available to all Apple HomeKit users. As it stands, you must have at least a 2nd generation HomePod, HomePod Mini or Apple TV 4K running Apple's latest operating system. You also need to use an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone, nominally the iPhone 15 Pro or later. But the biggest barrier is likely the price of the program's cloud storage, which could cost you up to $60 per month, depending on your number of cameras. For a list of compatible cameras, visit Apple's Smart Home Accessory website . Charging extra for a HomeKit Secure video cloud storage plan isn't anything new. Prior to the AI update, users could hook up a network of cameras using 50 GB, 200 GB, and 2 TB iCloud+ plans. However, the new AI features require you to pay for significantly more expensive iCloud+ plans. For just a single camera, for instance, you will need to invest in Apple's 2 TB iCloud+ plan, which will add $9.99 to your expenses. This monthly bill scales as you grow your home smart camera network. To operate a second Apple Intelligence-enabled camera, you'll need to upgrade to Apple's $29.99/month, 6 TB plan. Anything between 3 and the maximum 5 camera setup necessitates 12 TB of iCloud storage. This means that operating Apple Intelligence-enabled cameras around your home could cost a whopping $59.99 a month, meaning you may add more than $700 to your yearly household costs. Notably, this cloud storage is in addition your family's iCloud storage plan. Now, it's worth mentioning that you can enjoy the benefits of Apple Intelligence's HomeKit upgrades without deploying it across all your security cameras. For instance, you may want the AI summary feature for your front porch camera to track deliveries but may not find the same utility in analyzing the possum scurrying past your back window. Selectively deploying the feature may help reduce costs. However, its just as important to note that these prices aren't necessarily static. In its Apple Intelligence support page , Apple notes that supported cameras and iCloud+ features "may change over time." Given the volatile pricing of AI-ladened subscriptions as companies desperately seek out profitability, it's wise to view the consistency of these price structures with a dose of skepticism. Luckily, the feature is optional, so you won't be registered into a costly subscription if you don't plan on utilizing the feature. For now, anyway. If Apple's home surveillance AI summary tool seems worth the investment, you can set up your new AI-enabled security system directly in your iPhone, iPad, or Mac. First, make sure your HomeKit Secure Video system is set up on your iPhone or iPad by going to Settings > your name > iCloud > Show All, > Home . If using a Mac, go to the Apple menu > System Settings > Your name, located at the top of the sidebar. From there, click iCloud > See All, Show All, or Show More Apps > Home . To enable Home camera video descriptions, go to your iPhone's Home app. Next, tap the Home tab , hit the three dotted icon and select Home Settings . Here, you can turn on Apple Intelligence. Once completed, you can choose which cameras you would like to enable or disable the video descriptions feature for. If you want your HomeKit to recognize visitors from your camera roll, return to your iPhone's Home app . After adding your camera to your Home app's homepage, go to Recognize Familiar Faces , turn on Face Recognition , and tap Continue . To add recent visitors to your camera's catalog, go to the Home tab , tap the camera , and select the gear icon. Next, go t o Face Recognition , tap the unidentified person in your Recent list, and tap Add Name . Here, you can add appropriate identifiers and even choose whether you'd like to be notified whenever said person enters your camera view. To stop your smart home system from alerting you every time a racoon treks by, reduce your notifications through the Home app on your iPhone. Visit your system settings by going to Home > three dotted icon > Home Settings . Next, tap Apple Intelligence , and enable Reduce Notifications .

extraction.body: U.S. software development job postings have risen since February 2025, the launch date for Anthropic's Claude Code, even as overall job postings fell, complicating predictions that AI would rapidly erase demand for developers. Concerns about the future of the software development career are well-founded, and intensified as companies adopted AI-powered coding tools, especially as those tools keep getting better. As far back as 2023, Microsoft's software development platform GitHub said that on projects where AI was available, it was close to writing half of all code. Some AI experts claim AI-written code across the entire GitHub platform has now passed the halfway mark . GitHub has not confirmed that, but in October it did report that one in three "pull requests" — the process in which coders that collaborate on development propose code changes for projects — now involve an AI agent. A year ago, GitHub said that number was fewer than one in 10. "If that pace holds, within the next two years, most of the code pushed to GitHub could be written by an agent. Much of it may never be fully read by a human," it stated . Labor market researchers say that against this backdrop, the profession is evolving rather than disappearing. Data from Indeed Hiring Lab shows that U.S. software-development job postings have risen nearly 15% since February 2025, bucking both the overall job market and the coding data. Some economic experts are pointing to the rebound in software job postings as confirmation for a glass half-full view of AI and the job market. "It wasn't that long ago that we were reading the headline that there will be no more need for software developers," Eric Kutcher, North America chair at McKinsey, said during a recent interview on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Instead, he said, as companies are producing more code than ever before, software developers who work with AI remain in high demand. "We're seeing much more growth in the places we thought we were gonna see the biggest displacement," Kutcher said. Recent research on AI and the future of jobs from McKinsey Global Institute notes that the earlier decline in the software developer field was not solely an AI story. While in recent years AI has been automating software-development tasks, the rebound comes after a steep drop from a 2022 hiring peak, when technology companies pulled back after a pandemic-era surge in hiring. But even after the recovery, software-development job postings remain about 27.5% below their pre-pandemic level, according to Indeed Hiring Lab data . Importantly, the increase is concentrated in senior-level roles and more experienced AI-oriented positions. Indeed Hiring Lab found that senior roles accounted for 71% of the increase in software-development postings between May 2025 and May 2026. Job titles that mention AI accounted for 37% of the increase. AI tools may be allowing companies to produce code more quickly than developers could on their own. GitHub leaders have said in the past that as much if not more than 80% of code could eventually be written by AI, especially as developers become more comfortable working with AI tools. But that also could mean the demand for workers is concentrated on those who can evaluate AI-generated code or problems and connect new tools to an organization's broader technology systems. Sneha Puri, an economist at Indeed Hiring Lab, said companies are realizing that even if AI can handle some technical coding tasks, they still need developers to oversee that work, refine products and help clients integrate the technology into their day to day operations. One example, she said, is the growing need for workers who can help businesses apply AI tools beyond simply building them. Right now, factors like the ones cited by Puri are helping software developers to be among winners in the earliest stage of the AI transformation of the labor market. A recent analysis of U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data from economist Steve Rattner found that software developer was among the career categories that showed positive growth from May 2023 to May 2025, though it was merely in line with growth across all occupation and well below the pace of growth in traditionally blue-collar jobs associated with building AI data centers. Anthropic researchers found that even with automation, humans are still needed to oversee that automation and require user input. But the researchers cautioned that it is "by no means certain that this pattern will persist into the future." GitHub said in its report on pull requests that the as AI pushed more code into the world, and with it, more risks in the code, humans must be in a position to scale with the technology to police the AI's work. But that may not be possible forever. "As the amount of code grows, we must prevent more exposures and reduce the human effort required by those that remain, or else the volume of vulnerabilities introduced will become untenable," it wrote. For the youngest workers, the software development field outlook remains uncertain. Stanford University's 2026 AI index found that employment in AI-exposed fields for those aged 22 to 25 has fallen 16% since the rise of generative AI, with those identified as early-career software developers seeing a larger decline in employment of 20% as older developer roles expand. That shift has made the path into software development more difficult for recent graduates, even as demand rises for more experienced workers. Puri said students should build familiarity with AI tools but not neglect the skills that remain central when working with them. "Being able to use AI in your work and improve your efficiency is a great place to start," Puri said. "But communication, interpersonal skills and leadership are also really important," she added. Puri said employers also have a role to play in preserving routes into the field. "Today's entry-level talent becomes tomorrow's senior experts," she said. "If employers don't build those pipelines now, they're not going to have senior talent they need 10 years down the line." While forecasting job growth in the AI era is difficult, the long-term outlook for software developers remains positive, according to an August report from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. It projects employment of software developers will grow 10% from 2025 to 2035, increasing from about 1.72 million to 1.89 million jobs and adding roughly 174,700 positions. Concerns about the future of the software development career are well-founded, and intensified as companies adopted AI-powered coding tools, especially as those tools keep getting better. As far back as 2023, Microsoft's software development platform GitHub said that on projects where AI was available, it was close to writing half of all code.

Some AI experts claim AI-written code across the entire GitHub platform has now passed the halfway mark . GitHub has not confirmed that, but in October it did report that one in three "pull requests" — the process in which coders that collaborate on development propose code changes for projects — now involve an AI agent. A year ago, GitHub said that number was fewer than one in 10. "If that pace holds, within the next two years, most of the code pushed to GitHub could be written by an agent. Much of it may never be fully read by a human," it stated .

Labor market researchers say that against this backdrop, the profession is evolving rather than disappearing. Data from Indeed Hiring Lab shows that U.S. software-development job postings have risen nearly 15% since February 2025, bucking both the overall job market and the coding data.

Some economic experts are pointing to the rebound in software job postings as confirmation for a glass half-full view of AI and the job market. "It wasn't that long ago that we were reading the headline that there will be no more need for software developers," Eric Kutcher, North America chair at McKinsey, said during a recent interview on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Instead, he said, as companies are producing more code than ever before, software developers who work with AI remain in high demand. "We're seeing much more growth in the places we thought we were gonna see the biggest displacement," Kutcher said.

Recent research on AI and the future of jobs from McKinsey Global Institute notes that the earlier decline in the software developer field was not solely an AI story. While in recent years AI has been automating software-development tasks, the rebound comes after a steep drop from a 2022 hiring peak, when technology companies pulled back after a pandemic-era surge in hiring.

But even after the recovery, software-development job postings remain about 27.5% below their pre-pandemic level, according to Indeed Hiring Lab data . Importantly, the increase is concentrated in senior-level roles and more experienced AI-oriented positions. Indeed Hiring Lab found that senior roles accounted for 71% of the increase in software-development postings between May 2025 and May 2026. Job titles that mention AI accounted for 37% of the increase.

AI tools may be allowing companies to produce code more quickly than developers could on their own. GitHub leaders have said in the past that as much if not more than 80% of code could eventually be written by AI, especially as developers become more comfortable working with AI tools. But that also could mean the demand for workers is concentrated on those who can evaluate AI-generated code or problems and connect new tools to an organization's broader technology systems.

Sneha Puri, an economist at Indeed Hiring Lab, said companies are realizing that even if AI can handle some technical coding tasks, they still need developers to oversee that work, refine products and help clients integrate the technology into their day to day operations. One example, she said, is the growing need for workers who can help businesses apply AI tools beyond simply building them.

Right now, factors like the ones cited by Puri are helping software developers to be among winners in the earliest stage of the AI transformation of the labor market. A recent analysis of U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data from economist Steve Rattner found that software developer was among the career categories that showed positive growth from May 2023 to May 2025, though it was merely in line with growth across all occupation and well below the pace of growth in traditionally blue-collar jobs associated with building AI data centers.

Anthropic researchers found that even with automation, humans are still needed to oversee that automation and require user input. But the researchers cautioned that it is "by no means certain that this pattern will persist into the future."

GitHub said in its report on pull requests that the as AI pushed more code into the world, and with it, more risks in the code, humans must be in a position to scale with the technology to police the AI's work. But that may not be possible forever. "As the amount of code grows, we must prevent more exposures and reduce the human effort required by those that remain, or else the volume of vulnerabilities introduced will become untenable," it wrote.

For the youngest workers, the software development field outlook remains uncertain. Stanford University's 2026 AI index found that employment in AI-exposed fields for those aged 22 to 25 has fallen 16% since the rise of generative AI, with those identified as early-career software developers seeing a larger decline in employment of 20% as older developer roles expand.

That shift has made the path into software development more difficult for recent graduates, even as demand rises for more experienced workers. Puri said students should build familiarity with AI tools but not neglect the skills that remain central when working with them. "Being able to use AI in your work and improve your efficiency is a great place to start," Puri said. "But communication, interpersonal skills and leadership are also really important," she added.

Puri said employers also have a role to play in preserving routes into the field. "Today's entry-level talent becomes tomorrow's senior experts," she said. "If employers don't build those pipelines now, they're not going to have senior talent they need 10 years down the line."

passages: With the release of the Pixel 8 in 2023, Google made a widely celebrated announcement.
Going forward, Pixel phones would receive seven years of software updates — not only routine security patches but major OS upgrades, too.
A quick loss of software support had previously been a major reason why Android phones failed to hold their value for long, so committing to that support was crucial for the future.
If you want to keep your Pixel phone alive after Google kicks it off the update schedule, you have few options.
Of course, you can keep using it with the last software update it receives, but this will expose your phone to security risks in the long run.
Part of an Android phone's routine update schedule includes security patches , generally issued on a monthly cadence.
You should get a new phone if possible, or at least upgrade to one that still receives security updates.
That means the Pixel 7 and 7 Pro will get their final update by the end of October 2027, while the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro are currently reaching their end of support in October 2026.
Pixel a-series phones are released on a different cadence, so support windows differ accordingly.
Google's Pixel release date page is a helpful guide here.
First, all Pixels from the original model through the Pixel 5a are obsolete and no longer receiving updates.
You might assume that installing a custom ROM or OS image onto your old Pixel would give it new life after Google abandons it.

That's not to say you can't run DIY software on an out-of-service Pixel, but rather that any updates pushed to those projects will not benefit from original equipment manufacturer (OEM) firmware, kernel and vendor code.
Google begins the window of service for a given Pixel smartphone in the month it became available for purchase on the Google Store website in the US.
However, Lineage is still supporting the original Pixel from 2016, along with nearly every other Pixel phone since.
The Pixel 9a, which shipped in April 2025 after a March announcement, will receive no further updates after April 2032.
Google offers great support for Pixels, but not all models enjoy the full timeline.
